title: Akshay Kumar's 'Welcome' Jungle Opens to a Polite Roar — and the Weekend Will Decide Everything
excerpt: Past 10 crore by teatime, a 22-year Raveena reunion that stopped the set, and a holiday crowd carrying Welcome 3 on word of mouth. The numbers are in. The verdict isn't.
body:
The first thing you should know about **Welcome To The Jungle** is that the franchise was never about logic. It was about **Akshay Kumar** in a loud shirt, **Paresh Rawal** pretending to be a gangster who pretends to be a gentleman, and the entire ensemble screaming over each other until you give up and laugh. So when the third instalment finally stormed into cinemas this Friday — Muharram holiday, family crowds, the works — the only real question was whether the franchise still had the lungs for it.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=R704yP3dlXw</youtube>

Early answer: a polite roar, not yet a stampede.

By 11 AM on Day 1, the **Ahmed Khan**-directed comedy had collected around ₹2.36 crore net, opening to roughly 12% occupancy across India. By teatime the live tracker had it past ₹10 crore net, running across more than 6,000 shows. Add the ₹3.75 crore it banked in Thursday's paid previews — Bollywood's sixth-highest preview haul ever — and the film is comfortably on course for a ₹15-20 crore opening day, with the most optimistic trade voices whispering 23-27 crore once the night shows are counted.

> "#WelcomeToTheJungle: ENTERTAINING. Get ready for a 1980s-style masala entertainer... The focus is on fun, laughter, nostalgia, and larger-than-life entertainment – not logic or reasoning." — Taran Adarsh, ⭐️⭐️⭐️½

That's the verdict the makers wanted. After weeks of advance booking that whispered rather than roared, the film is being carried into the weekend on exactly the thing a Welcome movie runs on: word of mouth that says *don't think, just come.*

The ensemble, as ever, is the spectacle. **Akshay Kumar** anchors a cast that reads like a wedding guest list — **Suniel Shetty**, **Paresh Rawal**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Jacqueline Fernandez**, **Disha Patani**, **Lara Dutta**, **Johnny Lever**, **Rajpal Yadav**, **Krushna Abhishek**, **Kiku Sharda** and **Shreyas Talpade**, who is having quite the week (he's also in this Friday's *The India Story* teaser). But the moment that made the set stand up and clap was the return of **Raveena Tandon**, reuniting with Akshay 22 years after *Mohra* — a slow-dance of nostalgia the marketing has leaned on hard.

Geographically, the film is behaving like the mass entertainer it is. The morning numbers showed Lucknow and Jaipur leading occupancy at a blazing 31%, with the NCR belt (21%) edging out Mumbai (18.5%). The single-screen, non-metro heartland is where this film lives or dies, and so far the heartland is showing up.

It needs to. The competition ahead is brutal. **Cocktail 2** is still throwing punches after crossing ₹70 crore. And the runway is crowded with **Alpha** (July 3), **Dhamaal 4** (July 10) and **Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey** later in the summer — any one of which could swallow *Welcome's* screens whole. A Welcome film has never been built for the long haul; it's built for the first weekend, the holiday crowd, the families who want two and a half hours of zero homework. That weekend is now.

**For the diaspora:** *Welcome To The Jungle* opened in cinemas across North America, the UK and the Gulf this Friday alongside its India release — a near-simultaneous global rollout that's become standard for Akshay's holiday-window comedies. NRI audiences in the US and Canada can catch it at the usual desi-circuit multiplexes (AMC, Cinemark, Cineplex), with the Hindi original running with subtitles. An OTT landing — almost certainly on a major streamer within 6-8 weeks — will follow, but for a film engineered around a packed, laughing hall, the theatre is the whole point.

Here's the honest read: this isn't *Dhurandhar 2* money, and it was never going to be. It's a comfort-food franchise doing comfort-food numbers — decent, dependable, and entirely dependent on whether Saturday and Sunday families decide it's the film to take the kids to. The reviews call it nostalgic and silly in equal measure. The box office calls it open. The weekend gets the final word.

One thing's certain: after *Bhooth Bangla* and now this, Akshay Kumar has quietly rebuilt himself into the most reliable laugh-merchant in the business. Not the flashiest play in 2026. Possibly one of the smartest.
